title: Design System: Cashu

display.purpose: Short page-peak copy under ~25 characters: the closing-CTA slogan and the H1 on dedicated routes. The line break is part of the composition, not an accident of viewport.

heroDisplay.purpose: Retired 2026-08-14. Was a bespoke clamp(3.75rem, 7vw, 6.5rem) step for the homepage H1; it pinned at the bottom of the documented hero range and let the /wallets route H1 render 29-38% larger than the page peak. The hero now uses Display unmodified. Do not reintroduce a homepage-only display step.

footerDisplay.purpose: The compact closing wordmark. The footer's only Display type; the rest of that surface stays quiet.

title.purpose: Subheaders and card titles: the quiet side of Big-Or-Quiet.

brandWordmark.purpose: The navbar 'Cashu' letterform. Same face and tracking as the footer signoff mark, shrunk to bar scale, so the page opens and closes on one letterform.

body.purpose: All reading copy, capped at the 65-75 character measure.

heroLead.purpose: The homepage hero's supporting statement. Shares the hero grid width with text-wrap: pretty.

label.purpose: Navigation, captions, and the footer legal fields.

navLink.purpose: Bar links only. The current route steps to full Ink and one weight up, so colour is never the only signal.

button.purpose: Button labels only, uppercase. One step below Label so the all-caps slab reads as an object, not a line of text.

compactButton.purpose: The bar's own CTA and the mobile panel CTA, trimmed to sit comfortably in the row.

micro.purpose: The 'Fig. NN' caption register and the Figure/Code segmented-control labels.

mono.purpose: Code, addresses, and transaction ids: anywhere a literal copy-pasteable string appears in copy.

pixel.purpose: Protocol notation only: amounts, denominations, mint identifiers, version strings. Never a heading, eyebrow, section marker, or link affordance.

heroDeck.purpose: The standfirst under the hero headline: the page's claim in one line, sitting between Display and heroLead. Separated from the body on size, weight and tone at once so the two roles stay distinct at phone widths.

faceSubsetting.summary: All four faces are subset by scripts/subset-fonts.mjs: 134,904 bytes to 39,924. Geist Mono is a static wght=400 instance (5,188 bytes) rather than the full variable face (71,248).
faceSubsetting.constraint: A character outside the subset ranges does not tofu. It falls through the fallback chain to a system font and still looks correct, which is the defect that survives review. Verify by rasterising with the fallback chain stripped.
faceSubsetting.reRunWhen: geist is updated, a trial face is replaced, or the rendered character set changes: a keymap chord label, a NUT id, the hero field's alphabets, or copy outside Latin-1.
faceSubsetting.note: Ranges are deliberately wider than today's text. Per-face reasoning is in the script header. The hero field's atlas characters cannot be derived from the DOM because glyphs.ts draws them straight to a canvas.
faceSubsetting.location: assets/fonts/ holds the licensed masters and is never served. src/fonts/ holds the generated subsets, the only fonts a browser receives, since next/font/local copies them into _next/static/media/ with a content hash. Neither belongs under public/, which previously served all 13 masters at stable URLs nothing linked to and served each subset twice.

motion.name: ease-out-quart
motion.purpose: The system's ONLY curve as of 2026-08-20. Every state transition, entrance, draw and wipe on the site uses it. ease-out-quint (0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) and ease-out-expo (0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) sat beside it from the first motion pass and never acquired a consumer; they were deleted on the reasoning DESIGN.md section 2 used for --signal, since a token standing with no consumer is an invitation to reach for it without re-arguing the choice. A softer landing than quart should arrive with the surface that needs it and an argument for it.

motion.name: dur-fast
motion.purpose: Feedback: hover colour, focus, skip-link, and jump-arrival reveals.

motion.name: dur-base
motion.purpose: Button fill and border, mobile panel open, demo-view crossfade.

motion.name: dur-reveal
motion.purpose: The standard entrance settle: opacity plus an 8px rise. Scroll-triggered reveals run it as a transition gated on .is-revealed; unconditional ones run it as the reveal-arrival keyframe animation from parse time (see reveal-arrival below). As of 2026-08-20 the settled state is `transform: none`, not `translateY(0)`: the Focus-Pull Rule's first term applied to a third property — an entrance ends on the absence of what it animated, not on a neutral value of it — since translateY(0) left every settled reveal holding a containing block and a compositing hint. .reveal--fade and .reveal--instant already said none.

motion.name: reveal-arrival
motion.purpose: Entrances that always play (.reveal--arrival) as a CSS animation starting when the stylesheet parses, not on hydration. Same duration, easing, rise and stagger as the transition form. The 0.02 floor is load-bearing, not cosmetic: Chrome will not accept an element as an LCP candidate if its only main-thread paint has opacity exactly 0, and a composited opacity animation never repaints on the main thread, so from 0 the element stays invisible to the metric until hydration forces a repaint. Measured: LCP 2280ms before, 2244ms from 0, 648ms from 0.02. See the Set-Once Rule's second amendment in DESIGN.md section 4.

motion.name: dur-reveal-slow
motion.purpose: The slow entrance for large media and figure panels.

motion.name: reveal-focus
motion.value: blur(var(--reveal-blur)) to filter:none, cleared at 55% of the settle
motion.purpose: The focus pull (.reveal--focus): type arrives fractionally out of focus and resolves. Opt-in, never the default. Added 2026-08-19 on the user's direction; it is the site's only sanctioned blur and the only one that will ever be sanctioned, because it is a property of an entrance rather than a surface. Three terms are load-bearing. It ends on filter:none and never on blur(0px) — a settled blur(0) keeps a compositor layer and grayscale antialiasing on 9rem type for the life of the page. It clears at 55% so the rise lands under an already-sharp word and hero-cipher.tsx gets a sharp surface for the tail of its 760ms pass. It is a modifier because the masthead sits in a Reveal and a live canvas must not be wrapped in a filter. LCP measured either way on a throttled phone: 612/632ms with, 636/624ms without, same LCP element, CLS 0 — blur does not disqualify an LCP candidate the way opacity:0 does. See the Focus-Pull Rule in DESIGN.md section 4.

motion.name: reveal-blur
motion.value: 10px default; 18px hero headline, 12px route header, 9px hero deck, 6px section item, 4px hero CTA row
motion.purpose: Focus-pull radius, stated per consumer rather than globally. A radius is only meaningful against the type it softens: 18px is a hair of softness under a 9rem headline and an illegible smear under a 13px button label. Authored in globals.css with :has() against the composition's own class names, so the value sits next to its reasoning rather than inline in JSX.

motion.name: reveal-rise-section
motion.purpose: The below-the-fold rise, against the arrival's 8px. Under editorial type at this scale 8px reads as a twitch rather than a settle, which was the complaint that produced the group reveals. Transform-only movement contributes nothing to CLS, so the amplitude is free. See the Section-Gesture Rule in DESIGN.md section 4.

motion.name: dur-nav-wipe
motion.purpose: The masthead hover plate's clip-path wipe travelling across a nav label. Deliberately slower than dur-base: at feedback speed a travelling edge across a whole word reads as a flicker rather than a slide. (Replaces dur-nav/300ms, which documented the retired Onyx condense and had no consumers left; the dead token was removed from globals.css 2026-08-17.)

motion.name: hero-word-wipe
motion.purpose: One word of the hero headline uncovered left to right on arrival (.hero-wipe). Added 2026-08-19 on the user's direction, replacing the cipher pass that used to resolve it out of hex. Deliberately the masthead's own wipe at another scale: clip-path uncovering type is what the nav does under a hovered link and what hero-rule-draw does to the closing hairline, so the hero rhymes with the surfaces either side of it instead of introducing a third idea. It inherits --reveal-delay from the headline's Reveal wrapper, so it starts when the headline starts and ends at 580ms, inside the hairline's 1100ms. Two terms are load-bearing. It fills backwards rather than both — an entrance ends on the absence of what it animated, and both would leave a clip-path on the word for the life of the page: visually identical, and a permanent stacking context. The vertical insets are negative because the headline's line-height is 0.95, so the inline-block box is shorter than the type it sets and clipping at 0 shaves the caps. No JavaScript: a rule in the same stylesheet as the headline cannot arrive after the headline has, which is the entire problem hero-cipher.tsx existed to guard against.

motion.name: cipher-pass
motion.purpose: The button label's encrypt-to-decrypt sweep. Pointer only, never focus. Removed entirely under prefers-reduced-motion. ONE consumer as of 2026-08-19: the hero ran the same primitive decrypt-only over one word of the headline until the user cut it as corny and too on the nose. See hero-word-wipe below and the Set-Once Rule's third amendment in DESIGN.md section 4.

motion.name: dur-draw-on
motion.purpose: A line drawing itself. ONE consumer as of 2026-08-20: the hero's closing hairline, via clip-path. The second was .draw-on, SVG line art via stroke-dashoffset, which shared this duration because it was the same gesture at another scale; that rule set was deleted with the figures that used it (the ASCII field and the demo panel, both gone since 2026-08-16), and it took the stylesheet's only untokenized duration, a raw 480ms, with it. The token stays on its own consumer's account.

motion.name: reveal-group-wallets
motion.purpose: The wallets registry stagger (2026-08-20), applying the Section-Gesture Rule to the route the 2026-08-19 pass had skipped. Authored in globals.css keyed on .reveal-group .wallet-row:nth-child(), not as delay props — and that is the point rather than a preference: the props this replaced were 280 + gi*60 + i*50, which MAX_DELAY_MS clamped to a flat 360ms from the third row on, so the ladder was written, committed and silently thrown away. A delay expressed as a prop passes through a clamp it cannot see. 40ms a step, shorter than the arrival's, because a registry row is one line of type and the beat between two of them is shorter than the beat between a headline and a paragraph. The rows also take --reveal-blur-section 4px against the section default's 6px, on the same per-consumer reasoning as reveal-blur. The first group stays an arrival: its rail is above the fold at every viewport and a group is observer-gated, therefore hydration-gated. Net 21 client components and 21 observers to 6 and 3.

motion.name: sheet-open
motion.value: 220ms in (dur-base), 150ms out (dur-fast), ease-out-quart, clip-path inset top to bottom
motion.purpose: The ? help sheet opening and closing (2026-08-20). It was the only state change on the site with no transition at all. The material is the site's own travelling edge — the same clip-path uncovering the masthead plate, hero-rule-draw and .hero-wipe use — but it runs top to bottom rather than left to right, because left to right is how this site uncovers a WORD and this is a PANEL: the reference is the mobile nav sheet growing out of the bar, and a sideways wipe across a six-row table would uncover it column by column. The backdrop only fades; ground has no edge. The exit is the fast one in both properties, since a transition takes the duration of the state it is going to, so the base rule governs the close and [open] governs the open. display and overlay transition with allow-discrete, which is the whole reason an exit exists; @starting-style supplies the from-values for the open, since an element entering the top layer has no previous style. ONE COST, RECORDED: the settled [open] state holds clip-path inset(0 0 0 0), a standing clipping context — bounded to the time the sheet is open rather than the life of the page, and unavoidable for a wipe because inset() does not interpolate to none. Under reduced motion the wipe is cancelled and the fade kept.

motion.name: press-feedback
motion.value: scale(0.985) at 150ms on :active; hover treatments paired onto :focus-visible
motion.purpose: Feedback parity, 2026-08-20. .press-arrow was the only real <button> on the site with no pressed state; it takes the compression the .btn-* slabs already use, so no new value enters the system. The press cards lifted their photograph and wordmark on :hover and did nothing on :focus-visible, so the keyboard path got an outline and a photograph that did not answer — paired the way .site-nav__link already pairs the two. The hamburger is deliberately excluded: its icon already morphs to an X on activation, which is the same acknowledgement by other means.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Every animation on the site has a prefers-reduced-motion path, and the pattern is the button block's: remove the spatial movement, keep the colour, opacity and state change that carries the meaning. Three motions escaped it until 2026-08-20 — the skip link's translateY, the hamburger bars' rotate-and-move, and the mobile panel's grid-template-rows height animation — plus two JS counterparts: the g i chord's smooth scrollIntoView, and button-cipher.tsx, which read the query once at mount instead of live-tracking it as hero-field.tsx and orb-figure.tsx do. Each CSS cancel sits immediately after the rules it cancels, because the ties are decided on source order.

components.name: Primary Button (Flat Cipher Slab)
components.description: One of only two jobs a primary may serve: get a wallet, read the spec. Sharp, shadowless, all-caps.

components.name: Nav Link — The Wipe
components.description: White at 66% on the masthead's ink. Hover, :focus-visible, and the current route drive the plate across the link with clip-path over 460ms quart-out — the same --nav-plate the brand cell uses, so it is Paper by day and the page's near-black by night. The label is rendered twice — the base Paper-on-ink and an aria-hidden ink-on-Paper copy clipped to zero width — so the travelling edge passes through the letterforms and each one flips as it arrives. A single label cannot do this: its colour flips for the whole word at once, leaving the uncovered half invisible. A real element, not content: attr(), because screen readers announce generated content.

components.name: The Masthead
components.description: The whole navigation bar, rebuilt 2026-08-16 on the user's direction against a layout reference. Full-bleed, sticky, ink-ground, identical in every scroll state: a brand plate hard against the left edge, then one uninterrupted ink run to the right edge carrying the HH:MM UTC clock, the links and the marks. The plate follows the scheme — --nav-plate is --paper and its text is --ink, so it is the page punched through the bar rather than a fixed white slab. Two features of the reference shipped and were rejected on sight the same day and must not come back: an open slot column mid-bar (it read as a hole punched in the bar) and a pixel-dither strip along the bottom edge (it read as noise under it). It replaced the Onyx two-state bar, whose condensed glass box was the system's only glass, radius, and shadow surface — all three exceptions are now closed. Ground is #18181b in light and #3f3f46 in dark: the plate is always --paper, so the bar has to be the value that contrasts with it in both schemes.

components.name: Hairline Divider
components.description: A single 1px line in Hair at full content width. The only structural divider in the system: no double rules, no decorative rules, no vertical dividers.

components.name: Pixel Notation
components.description: The system's one typographic flourish, and it earns its place semantically: pixel type marks machine data inside human prose.
components.html: A single proof carries 2048 sat, signed by keyset 00ffd48b8f5ecf80.
components.css: .ds-prose { font-family: var(--font-gt), ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 400; line-height: 1.5; color: var(--body); margin: 0; } .ds-pixel { font-family: var(--font-pixel), var(--font-mono), monospace; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 500; line-height: 1; letter-spacing: 0.04em; color: var(--ink); }

components.name: Status Tag (Signal Square)
components.description: The wallet-directory status tag: a 7px --signal-page square, 8px, then one word in uppercase Mono tracked 0.06em, on the page ground. The square is the site's ONLY chromatic mark in its own voice (§2, the Signal-Green Exception) and it opens a stated property — maturity ("Beta"), which is a different class of fact from surface ("iOS and Android"). It is aria-hidden and decorative, so it never carries meaning alone: the word states the fact. Sharp and flat like every other object in the system — no fill, no border, no padding, no radius, no shadow. The recipe came from the protocol-parts property lists, which had the same square on the always-dark column in --signal (#6fe3a4); those lists were cut 2026-08-18 on the user's direction and the --signal token was deleted with them, so this is now the whole exception rather than half of it. The square is an inline-block ::before on the text baseline (lifted 1px, centring it against the 12px cap height) so the tag keeps a baseline and sits on the facts row with its mono siblings.
components.css: .ds-tag { font-family: var(--font-mono), ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, monospace; font-size: 0.75rem; letter-spacing: 0.06em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--ink); white-space: nowrap; } .ds-tag::before { content: ''; display: inline-block; width: 7px; height: 7px; margin-right: 8px; margin-bottom: 1px; background-color: var(--signal-page); }

components.name: Registry Row
components.description: One line per directory entry on /wallets, hairline-separated across three tracks: wordmark plus destination host, decision facts in their own column so they align down the page, and a single Open control. The name is a label, not a second link — the row spends one tab stop, not two.

components.name: Twilight Stack (Closing Band)
components.description: The system's one atmospheric flourish, reserved for the closing CTA and footer. An Ink band under a monochrome bloom anchored below the lower edge, plus a fractal-noise paper grain. Text in the lower third is contrast-checked against the bloom, never against the section's declared black — which is why the disclaimer is Hair, not Fog.
components.html:
Cashu

The open specification.

Mints are operated by independent parties; balances held with a mint are a claim on that mint, not a deposit. Read the spec before trusting anyone, including us.

components.name: Prose Link
components.description: The site's one inline text link, for a sentence that cites a source rather than restating it. Ink text with a 1px Mist underline at 0.2em, strengthening to Ink on hover. No colour (a blue link opens the palette the No-Colour Rule closes) and no glyph (the Don't list rules out `Visit →` and arrows). Mist rather than Fog because here the underline is the affordance: 4.8:1 on Paper against Fog's 2.3:1. NO CONSUMER TODAY (2026-08-18): its only one was the wallets page's citation of cashubtc/nuts, which the user cut. The rule and the CSS are kept as the recipe for any future prose citation — the alternative to having it on hand is the blue link or the `Visit →` it exists to rule out.
components.html: Optional NUT support varies between wallets. The spec repo tracks which implementations support what.

narrative.overview:
THE SITE IS LIGHT ONLY (user-directed 2026-08-17): no dark mode, no prefers-color-scheme branch, no data-theme override, no toggle. That is not the same as having no dark surfaces — the Twilight Stack, the protocol-parts column, the masthead and the Spec pane are fixed-value dark plates on a light page, and the implementations Card is a fixed light one. cashu.space dresses an open protocol in the visual register of a published RFC. Tight grid, fixed-width-quoted accents, monumental display type, and almost nothing decorative. The site reads as primary-source material — not a marketing page for a coin, not a fintech dashboard, not a Web3 launchpad. Visitors should feel they are looking at *the* document for Cashu, the way bitcoin.org once felt like *the* document for Bitcoin.

The system commits to a few sharp moves: massive editorial display type (GT-Standard) carries the page; neutrals stay pure (ink-on-paper, no tint, no warmth); structural elements are minimal — a thin horizontal rule, a pair of sharp-cornered buttons, generous whitespace. The Geist Pixel accent exists for one purpose: to mark machine-coded artefacts (token amounts, mint addresses, version numbers) when the spec calls for a notation different from prose. Cashu is not a SaaS, so the system actively rejects SaaS-landing-page chrome: no gradient borders, no soft drop shadows, no animated tickers, no testimonial carousels, and no glassmorphism anywhere at all — the navbar was the one sanctioned surface until 2026-08-16, and the masthead that replaced it is flat opaque ink.

Motion is permitted under one condition: it must depict real protocol structure, or be plain material carrying no assertion at all. The hero's ground is a live ASCII field — a contour heightfield drawn in Geist Mono glyphs — that fills the section and cycles slowly between open terrain, a vault door, and a schematic of the blind-signature round trip that Cashu actually performs. It does not answer the pointer: a contour lens that bent the sampling around the cursor was removed 2026-08-16 (user-directed) because over a full-bleed hero it read as a smear across the headline's ground. The field is weather, not a control. Never a decorative flow, never a connection the protocol doesn't make, and never a hover response. See the Honest-Network Rule in §4, and `src/lib/ascii/` for the field itself.

Color is intentionally absent from everything the site says in its own voice. The palette is paper, ink, and a graded family of greys. This is a doctrine, not a placeholder. The bitcoin-curious audience reads sovereignty in restraint; any added accent would dilute the signal. Two carve-outs, both named in §2: the Depicted-World Exception, which lets artifacts the page *depicts* (now only third-party marks) keep their source colour; and the Signal-Green Exception, added 2026-08-16 on the user's direction, which puts one green in one shape — a 7px square opening a stated property, in the protocol-parts column and on the wallet-directory status tag — and nowhere else, and never at scale.
keyCharacteristics: Monochrome by doctrine: paper, ink, six grades of grey, no chromatic accent.
Display type does the heaviest lifting: GT-Standard at 6rem–9rem on the hero, set tight (line-height 0.95, letter-spacing −0.02em).
Generous editorial whitespace; sections breathe at 80–128px vertical rhythm on large screens.
Sharp flat-slab buttons, hairline dividers, and no shadows — hierarchy comes from fill, border, position, and weight.
Cashu's protocol artefacts (amounts, ids, addresses) are set in Geist Pixel Square as a deliberate notation contrast.

rules.name: The Two-CTA Rule
rules.body: Primary buttons across the site exist to serve two jobs and two only: *get a wallet* and *read the spec*. These are the outcomes PRODUCT.md elevates above mint trust, and the visual hierarchy follows. Every other interactive surface — GitHub, blog, tab switchers, secondary navigation — is a `.btn-secondary` or a `nav-link`. If a third "primary" CTA appears on a single page the page is competing with itself; collapse one before shipping.

rules.name: The No-Colour Rule
rules.body: The system uses no chromatic accent. Greys may shift by lightness but never by hue. If a future surface "needs" colour, the design is wrong — work the hierarchy with type and space before reaching for a swatch.

rules.name: The Depicted-World Exception
rules.body: Colour is permitted inside artifacts the page *depicts*, never in the chrome the site *is*. The sanctioned surface is now one: third-party marks shown at their brand identity — the language logos on the implementations card and the AI-assistant icons in the footer. Narrowed 2026-08-16 on the user's direction: surface (a) was the tap-to-pay video, and the video band was deleted outright, so the exception loses its founding case and keeps only the marks. Everything in the site's own voice — type, backgrounds, borders, buttons, icons, figures, chrome — stays monochrome. Editorial photography *reports* rather than depicts, so it still desaturates via `grayscale(1) contrast(1.05)` and its wordmarks force to Paper (see the press band). A new colour surface that is not a third-party mark falls under the No-Colour Rule, or under the Signal-Green Exception if it is literally the mark that exception names.

rules.name: The Signal-Green Exception
rules.body: Added 2026-08-16 on the user's direction, overriding the No-Colour Rule for exactly one mark, and widened the same day to a second consumer of it. NARROWED BACK TO ONE CONSUMER 2026-08-18, user-directed: the protocol-parts property lists were cut, .protocol-part__mark went with them, and the --signal token (#6fe3a4, the mint picked against the always-dark column) was deleted rather than left in :root unused — an unused chromatic token in a monochrome system is how a bounded exception widens by accident. ONE licensed consumer and no others: the 7px square on the wallet-directory status tag (.wallet-row__fact--tag::before) in --signal-page (#1b9d55, 3.50:1 on Paper). This is the only chromatic value the site uses in its own voice, and unlike the Depicted-World Exception it depicts nothing. It is ::before content with no accessible name, sharp and flat (radius 0, no shadow, no gradient, no soft alpha), and it opens a stated property — the word states the fact, the square only marks it as a different class of fact. Never type, a fill, a glow, a gradient, a hover, a focus ring, or a success/error state. SCALE IS THE WHOLE EXCEPTION: the largest instance anywhere is 7 pixels square. It was briefly widened a third time to the hero's pointer plume and narrowed back the same day, user-directed — at hero scale it was the largest chromatic event on a monochrome page, carried no information, and read as the pastel/Web3 register the anti-references rule out; the mint came from aspensearch.com, and a borrowed accent at full-bleed is the other site's signature on your page. The exception has been widened three times and narrowed three times and now sits on one square, on one row, on one page. Weigh any future consumer by area first. If a fixed dark ground ever needs this square again, measure a value against that ground rather than reaching back for the deleted mint.

rules.name: The Two-Black Rule
rules.body: Ink (`#000000`) and Ink Soft (`#18181b`) are the only two text colours that may sit on Paper. Slate / Mist / Fog exist for legal disclaimers, nav, and labels only — never for primary reading copy.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: GT-Standard carries everything readable. Geist Mono is technical notation; Geist Pixel Square is protocol notation. Three families, three jobs, no overlap.

rules.name: The Big-Or-Quiet Rule
rules.body: Type is either Display (≥3.75rem) or quiet (≤1.125rem). The middle ground — `text-2xl` / `text-3xl` body — is avoided. Hierarchy is achieved by jumping scale, not by stair-stepping.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: `box-shadow` is forbidden throughout the site, including buttons. If a surface needs separation, use spacing, fill contrast, or a 1px border. No exceptions. From 2026-07-25 to 2026-08-16 the navbar's condensed box carried `--nav-shadow` as part of the Onyx scroll behaviour; the masthead that replaced it has no box to lift, the token is deleted, and the rule is absolute again.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Structural separation between sections is achieved with a single 1px line in Hair (`#e4e4e7`), full content width, never bolder. No double rules, no decorative rules.

rules.name: The Fold-Line Rule
rules.body:
The hero fills one viewport height (`min(100svh - var(--nav-h), var(--hero-max))`) and reads as a spec cover: title at the top, horizon at the bottom, the closing hairline resolving *on* the fold rather than floating above it with dead ground below. Two bounds keep it honest: `--nav-h` is subtracted because the bar is sticky and occupies flow space, and `--hero-max` (1200px) stops the chase on very tall displays, where an uncapped hero would open a void instead of a horizon. Past the cap the next section peeks in, which is the intended degradation.

*Amended 2026-08-14, on the user's direction.* The ASCII field was a `clamp(180px, 26vh, 320px)` band pinned to the section's base; it is now a full-bleed layer filling the hero, with the copy sitting on top of it. **The rule's substance is unchanged — only its mechanism is.** "Title at the top, horizon at the bottom" is now enforced by the field's mask rather than by the band's height: a vertical gradient holds the field fully transparent behind the sticky bar and near-transparent through the headline, and a horizontal gradient holds the field down through the middle of the section where the copy sits, so it runs at full strength out to both edges and frames the column instead of sitting behind it. That density gradient is load-bearing composition and must not be "corrected" by flattening the mask to uniform. The old prohibition on growing the band is retired with the band.

*Corrected later the same day:* the horizontal mask was a one-sided **left** dimmer while the hero copy was left-aligned. It is symmetric now — see the Centred-Hero Exception below. The two are a matched pair: if the hero ever goes back to left-aligned, the mask has to go back to one-sided or it will quiet the wrong side.

rules.name: The Centred-Hero Exception
rules.body:
*Added 2026-08-14, on the user's direction.* The homepage hero is centred: `.hero-spec__content` runs `align-items: center` with `text-align: center`, and the headline, deck, lead and CTA row all centre on the page axis.

**This is a deliberate departure and the only one on the site.** Everything else — every section heading, the wallets registry, the implementations directory, the footer, both interior routes — stays left-aligned editorial, which is what PRODUCT.md's "editorial-minimal, confident through silence" describes and what the rest of the system is built for. A centred hero sits closer to the marketing register than the rest of the page does. That was weighed and chosen, not drifted into.

Do not "restore" the hero to left-aligned as a consistency fix, and do not spread centring outward to the sections beneath it. If it ever does go back, three things move together or the composition breaks:

1. **The optical-left corrections come back.** Glyph side bearing has to be cancelled against a left margin: measured for GT-Standard 600, the headline needs `-0.058em` (round cap "O") and the deck and lead `-0.095em` (flat caps "I", "E"). Without them the inked left edge staggers four ways — up to 8px at display sizes, and worse as the type grows. See the Fold-Line Rule above.
2. **The field's horizontal mask goes back to one-sided.** It is symmetric now so it quiets the middle where centred copy sits; against left-aligned copy it would dim the wrong side.
3. **The headline's width escape may no longer be needed.** It currently sizes off the viewport rather than the page shell (`min(calc(100vw - 2 * var(--page-x)), 1440px)`) because the shell capped it at 1088px while the line needs ~1283px to break in two, orphaning "bitcoin." on its own line.

rules.name: The Honest-Network Rule
rules.body:
Network visualisations and motion are permitted *only when they reflect real protocol structure*. Acceptable: Lightning Network bridges shown as animated dotted lines between mint markers; peer-to-peer token transfer between users. Forbidden: decorative flow, speculative connections, "mints talking to mints" (which Cashu doesn't do), or any animation that exists for aesthetic energy rather than to convey a true property of the protocol. When in doubt, the simpler static version is more honest than the animated one.

*Amended 2026-08-14, on the user's direction, for the hero ASCII field.* The field cycles slowly (92s) between three named scenes, and each clears the rule on its own terms:

- **Terrain** is a contour heightfield. It depicts nothing and claims nothing — it is a material, like paper grain. Texture is outside the rule's scope; the rule governs things that assert a structure.
- **The vault door** is a depicted object, not a network. It carries no edges and implies no topology.
- **The blind-signature round trip** *is* protocol structure, and is the scene that earns the motion: Alice's secret stays on her side, the blinded point travels out, the mint signs without seeing it, the signature returns, and the secret plus the signature resolve into a bearer token. Two nodes, one round trip, no third party. The travelling dashes are the same device the rule already blesses for Lightning bridges.

What stays forbidden is unchanged and explicit: no mint-to-mint edge, no speculative connections, no third node standing in for "the network", and no scene added to the cycle purely because it would look good. A world map was proposed and rejected on exactly this ground — it asserts a global reach the protocol does not itself claim.

*Recorded waiver, same date.* The `$ ¥ €` glyphs on high contours and `₿` at the peaks (`terrain.ts`) depict no protocol structure; the 2026-07-26 critique flagged this. It is retained as the site's own voice and the ₿ density was deliberately increased (`PEAK_BOOST`). Noted here so it is a decision rather than an oversight.

rules.name: The Legible-Rim Rule
rules.body: On a flat, shadowless system the 1px rim *is* the control — nothing else marks a secondary button as pressable. It therefore carries a real boundary, not a decorative one: Mist at rest, never Hair. Hair (`#e4e4e7`) measures 1.27:1 against Paper and Slate (`#3f3f46`) measures 2.01:1 against Ink, both under WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11's 3:1 for a control's identifying boundary; at those values "READ THE SPEC" read as a line of text with a ghost around it. Restraint is a tonal choice about *which* grey, never a licence to drop below the threshold that makes the control a control. The rule is about rims, not about buttons, and binds every outlined control on the site. The press pager was the case that proved it: an `rgba(255,255,255,0.25)` rim composites to `#404040` on Ink — 2.03:1, the identical failure, on a control that isn't a `.btn-*`. It now carries Mist at rest and Fog on hover, the same two tones as `.btn-secondary--on-ink`. Any new outlined control inherits this before it inherits anything else.

rules.name: The Set-Once Rule
rules.body: The hero sets once and then holds, and its only other motion is the one the reader causes. The arrival: the closing hairline draws across the fold, one word of the headline resolves out of hex, and the copy settles on the staged reveal; by roughly 1.1s nothing is moving. AMENDED 2026-08-16 (user-directed, after aspensearch.com) when the hero got a ground again — hero-field.tsx, a frozen field of Geist Mono hex whose occupancy is Perlin noise, with a monochrome wake the pointer stirs through it. Two alphabets: hex at rest (entropy, which is what a Cashu secret is) and currency marks inside the wake (BTC weighted 6-in-16, then $ EUR JPY KRW GBP INR RUB cent PHP UAH), re-encrypting behind it. Nothing cycles — each cell has one resting digit and one denomination, both hashes of its coordinates. U+20BF and U+20A9 are .notdef in Geist Mono and are drawn from the face's own letterforms, not typed. (It shipped that afternoon as a Bayer dither with a mint plume and was rebuilt the same evening, user-directed, for being too close a copy of the reference. The terms below admitted a ground in the first place and did not change.) The clause struck was 'no hover response'; what survives is the rule's actual argument, which is that motion must be CAUSED. The terms: the field never drifts (no time uniform exists in the shaders); there is no requestAnimationFrame at rest (the loop starts on pointermove, stops ~2.2s after the last one, and window.__heroFieldFrames makes that testable); it stops on a frame bit-identical to the resting one; and the SOLVER is never allocated under prefers-reduced-motion or without a fine hover pointer, though the still GROUND mounts for everyone — withholding a frozen texture from someone who asked for less motion would withhold it for no reason, and gating it on a mouse would hand every phone a different hero. Still forbidden: ambient background animation, idle cycles, timers, parallax, and any hero motion the reader has not caused. A figure that depicts real protocol structure remains admissible under the Honest-Network Rule's first branch; the hex field is a GROUND, not a figure, and stands on the second branch only.

rules.name: The Brand-Mark Exemption
rules.body: The Cashu mascot is a full-colour raster in the masthead on every route, and no named rule covered it: the Depicted-World Exception is scoped to third-party marks and Signal-Green names one 7px square, so §2 as written forbade the site's own logo. It is exempt because it is the identity the rest of the system expresses. Exactly one asset at its shipped colours: not a licence for a coloured wordmark, a second mascot pose, or a value sampled out of the mascot and used elsewhere.

dos: Do carry the No-Colour Rule. Greys may shift by lightness, never by hue.
Do set the hero headline in Display (GT-Standard 600, ≥3.75rem, line-height 0.95). The headline earns the page.
Do keep body copy at 65–75ch max width. Long reads are an editorial feature, not an accident.
Do let the footer disclaimer span the complete footer grid. It is the deliberate exception to the prose measure, closing the composition on the same edges as the rows above.
Do use Geist Pixel Square only for protocol notation (amounts, ids, version strings). It is signal, not style.
Do name implementations by name. Cashu is a directory; wallets and mints appear as plain wordmarks, no logos required at first pass.
Do treat 1px Hair lines as the only structural divider. Sections separate by space first, hairline second.
donts: Don't introduce chromatic accent in the site's own voice. Generic crypto landing pages are the anti-reference — neon gradients on black, gradient text, animated 3D coins. Never on cashu.space. Colour appears in exactly two places, both named in §2: third-party marks, under the Depicted-World Exception; and the signal green on the 7px squares that open a stated property (the protocol-parts property lists and the wallet-directory status tag), under the Signal-Green Exception — a scoped licence for one mark doing one job, not a palette slot, and never at scale.

Don't add Web3 / DeFi tropes: pastel gradients, blob shapes, decorative network animations that misrepresent how the protocol works (e.g. mints "talking" to mints, which Cashu doesn't do). Motion is permitted only under the Honest-Network Rule — see §4.
Don't dress up privacy. No locks, no shields, no padlocks, no ALL-CAPS "YOUR DATA, SECURED™" copy. Privacy is a property of the protocol, stated plainly.
Don't use `box-shadow` anywhere. No drop shadow, inner shadow, coloured glow, or button exception.
Don't use `border-left` / `border-right` >1px as a coloured stripe on cards or callouts. Side-stripes are forbidden in impeccable's universal bans and doubly forbidden here.
Don't use `background-clip: text` with a gradient (gradient text). One solid colour, emphasis by weight or size.
Don't introduce a third typeface. Three families exist (GT-Standard, Geist Mono, Geist Pixel Square) and each has one job.

Don't use Geist Pixel Square as a section eyebrow, RFC-style metadata label, or link affordance. The pixel face marks protocol artefacts inside prose; everywhere else it reads as decoration. Section eyebrows in general are out — sections separate by space and headline, not by labelled introductions.
Don't centre body copy. Long-form reading sets flush left, ragged right.
Don't use stock photography of smiling teams, abstract blockchain visuals, or any hero treatment that could appear unchanged on a fintech site.
Don't ship Chalk placeholder surfaces in final layouts. They are scaffolding only.

handPatchNote: Hand-patched, not regenerated. 2026-08-20: motion extensions updated for the /impeccable animate pass — removed ease-out-quint, ease-out-expo and draw-on (all deleted from globals.css with their consumers), added reveal-group-wallets, sheet-open, press-feedback and reduced-motion, and amended ease-out-quart, dur-draw-on and dur-reveal. See DESIGN.md section 4.
